Episode 258. The Predator of All Dimensions (13)
The sky was blazing.

Kelliark Zipple. He flaunted his magic as if he had never been tired. Although the darkness Helluram had spread still remained across the entire battlefield, it alone could not completely offset the heat of the Annihilation Flame Orb.
Kiiiiik-!
A sharp, deafening sound, like metal scraping, echoed. It was a sound that began as the central part of the Flame Orb opened like an eye and a single spear protruded from within.
Without a moment to block it, the spear fell towards Laprarosa's upper armor.
If Malugia hadn't amplified the sun energy of Beltian, who was protecting Laprarosa's power at that moment, it wouldn't have ended with just the armor being torn off.
Kudud, dddd-deuk...!

The upper armor, having barely withstood the blow, poured down to the ground like a rotten shell. The shockwave alone created huge pits all over the ground, and those who had lost consciousness or died fell helplessly into them.
Still, Kelliark did not distinguish between friend and foe.

As if it didn't matter at all if the Demon Army was annihilated as long as Laprarosa was destroyed, he paid no mind to his own subordinates who were in the path of the attack. Not just the fleet, but also the Genesis Knights and even the phoenixes and gods he had summoned.
[Ugh...! The workshop, how is the Lady of the Secret Palace!?]
"Fortunately, the Lady of the Secret Palace's seal was not damaged! But if another impact of this magnitude is transmitted, I cannot guarantee it then...!"
The workshop of Ameris and Rokia, and the grand sealing of Talaris spread to protect it.

If the grand sealing were to break from the impact, the Coalition would truly have only one chance left. There would be no other means to protect Ameris and Rokia from the impact, so from that point on, they would have to fight in a state where the curse removal could fail at any moment.
"Now it really feels like a fight. Death flickers before my eyes every moment, and goosebumps rise on my skin."
Between the opened Flame Orb, the next spear was already appearing. Amidst the terrible metallic screech, Kelliark's madness-filled laughter was buried.
"Chiron!"
It was Van. She and Chiron were already leaping into the sky to intercept the spear, spraying sword energy.
Helluram still needed time to recover. Instead, Malugia, Haylin, and a barely-conscious Kragos were also seen throwing themselves to check the Flame Orb.

Chiron and Van's sword energy struck the center of the Flame Orb first. For a moment, the tip of the giant spear was seen denting, and immediately after, the sun energy shot by the Sun God's egos spread out in three strands like chains and bound the Flame Orb.
The Flame Orb was not made solely of Kelliark's magic. It was a weapon in which a part of his body and true energy were entirely melted.

Therefore, every time the Flame Orb was hit, Kelliark coughed up a viscous clot of blood and bent at the waist. But even as he had a seizure as if he would stop breathing at any moment, Kelliark glared at Laprarosa until the very end.
"Hehehe, you can't stop it like this. If that thing falls, you too will become a handful of dirt, one by one."
It had only momentarily lost its shape from the impact; the spear was stubbornly pushing its way out of the Flame Orb.
Moreover, an even stronger and harder energy could be felt than before. It was because it had absorbed some of the aura, lightning energy, and sun energy that had just struck the Flame Orb.
A choice had to be made.

It was a moment that required Luet's choice, not the Genesis Knights fighting in the crucible. Whether to take another blow from the spear in place, or to dodge it. The situation was too urgent to ask for Jin's opinion.

If they dodged, the spear would naturally fall to the ground. To the allies who were under Laprarosa's protection. Most of them would disappear into a handful of ash in an instant before that great power, without even being able to scream, without knowing why.
[...Commencing evasive maneuvers. Use every possible means to avoid the attack.]

Luet made an immediate decision. Having already faced the same dilemma once, she had decided to move then as well. It was only thanks to Helluram's appearance that he had been able to catch his breath for a moment.
Having seen Kelliark cornered with his own eyes just before, he too wanted to hold on and protect his allies as much as possible if she could.

But there was no guarantee that the battle in the crucible would end in the allies' victory. It seemed like Kelliark could fall at any moment, but that was just how it looked. He was showing a power stronger than at any other time since the battle began.
I'm sorry.
Luet gritted her teeth, swallowing his next words. As Laprarosa rapidly ascended, the spear struck the ground spread out beneath it.
For a moment, Jin almost looked back.
Death.
So much death.
The countless Coalition members who had come to contribute even a little to the decisive battle, to hold back even one more enemy.

About half of them were buried by Kelliark's spear and turned into a handful of ash in an instant. The countless deaths, the expressions on their faces at the end, their gazes, were assailing Jin's inner self as if they had happened right before his eyes.
He had to get a grip.
If he showed even a momentary opening, crushed by his inner pain, Kelliark's evil grasp would never miss that moment. Fortunately, Jin's sword was still aimed forward.
Kelliark grinned as if finding that sight admirable.

"As expected, you don't disappoint me. Well, it's really a small number compared to the number of Demon Army members you've killed, but it's been a long time since making someone suffer has been this joyful."
Not everyone on the ground had died.
It was thanks to Murakan and the Coalition's superhumans who had fought desperately to somehow fill the spot Laprarosa had left.
[Ice Princess, are you alright!]
"To call me by that name even in this situation... Hurry up and shout for everyone to scatter, Murakan. We don't know when that thing will suddenly fall again..."
Syris said, spitting out blood foam. Lucy, who was next to her, had five fist-sized holes pierced through her body but was slowly recovering.
This time too, the Plutonian had taken the biggest hit. It was the price for sacrificing themselves to protect their allies.
"Lord Linpa!"
It was Mary.
She hadn't been able to put up a shield when the spear fell. It was because she was already being pressured by a Demon Army Genesis Knight.
The moment she thought she was dead, Linpa had appeared in front of her. She had several large holes pierced through her body to protect Mary, but she couldn't recover like Lucy.
"Why me? Lord Linpa, you're stronger than me...!"
"What's... so... important... about that, Mary."
Linpa caressed Mary's face once, then took out her own rattling Light-Heart from her chest and handed it to her.
"A brother's... brother is... a brother."
Her characteristic slow speech. Linpa grimaced several times to try and leave her last words as quickly as possible. But after handing over the Light-Heart, she smiled and said this.
"We... live... by the heart."
Linpa's eyes closed. Mary hugged her tightly once, then had no choice but to leave.

But she didn't leave alone. What's so important about that? Those words were echoing in her head. The Flame Orb was spewing its next spear, but Mary was helping the fallen to their feet and moving on, taking in the dead with her eyes.
When she passed by the dead comrades like that, for some reason, a golden energy remained in their place. It was the Authority of Regeneration that Jin possessed.
It wasn't a phenomenon that only happened to Mary. Whoever took the dead into their hearts, a golden energy bloomed in every place they had passed.
Resonance.
The Authority of Regeneration was resonating with everyone in the Coalition. The comrades were facing the deaths that Jin was deliberately ignoring for the sake of the fight.

After the spear fell, the one who was saving the most Coalition members was Eltiot. He was still commanding the battlefield with the power of harmony, and a wind that sounded like a sad dirge was blowing in tune with him.

Everyone was facing their sorrow head-on. Except for the Genesis Knights in the crucible who were trying to maintain their extreme senses for the fight, everyone in the Coalition was carrying the still-unextinguished lives and the unavoidable deaths in tune with Eltiot's wind.
"...Young Miss!?"

Hedo, who was standing in the middle of it all, turned around at the familiar energy he suddenly felt. Sandra Zipple, the young miss he had served more preciously than his own life, was standing there. She was wearing a subtle expression that even Hedo had never seen before.
"It's dangerous, why did you leave Laprarosa!?"
"Hedo, come to think of it, I'm close to immortal. I have to save my darling's people."
"You can't, Young Miss. Your attributes too, against Kelliark's magic..."
"Shut up. I'm too weak to help Jin directly, and you're telling me to just keep watching his people die like this? Sitting inside Laprarosa, the safest place here? Let's go, quickly."

Hedo couldn't stop her. Sandra was already running on the ground that was boiling like water due to the heat of the Flame Orb. It was a heat that couldn't be offset for even a moment with the magic she possessed. She had already had her ankles melt and regenerate a dozen times while coming near Hedo.
"H-help me..."

There were also many enemies who had barely survived and were begging for their lives. They were groaning, saying they wanted to go home or see their families, like ordinary soldiers on any battlefield.
But they did not save each other.

To be precise, they couldn't. The Demon Army's Genesis Knights were already taking cover and catching their breath, and Rondo, who commanded them, was trying to stick to Laprarosa like a hound with the remaining Genesis Knights and gods.
While those trying to embrace each other somehow and those trying to bite until the very end somehow were wandering the battlefield avoiding the heat.
The Flame Orb was spewing spears without rest, and soon the seventh spear was aiming for Laprarosa.
The speed at which it was taking out the spears was slowing down a little. However, the Genesis Knights and the Sun God's egos were also losing their stopping power by that much.
And beyond the dimensional gate, in the complexly intertwined dimensional passages, the blackened Origin Stone was flying towards the battlefield.
There was no one on the battlefield who could stop it.
